label: [RELEASED]
claim: Linux 7.1.3 is the current stable release as of 2026-07-18 and does not contain USB4STREAM.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: Linux 7.2-rc3 is the current mainline prepatch as of 2026-07-18 and contains USB4STREAM.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: USB4STREAM entered Linus’s tree through the signed thunderbolt-for-v7.2-rc1 tag and usb-7.2-rc1 merge.

label: [EVIDENCE-GAP]
claim: The exact object IDs of each of the ten individual USB4STREAM series commits were not independently recovered; the signed tag target, merge commit, message IDs and exact subjects are pinned.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: CONFIG_USB4_STREAM is a tristate depending on USB4_CONFIGFS and builds thunderbolt_stream.ko.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: The public ABI is ConfigFS plus a misc character device /dev/tbstreamX; no ioctl UAPI is implemented.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: Each configured stream exposes index, in_hopid, out_hopid, ring_size and throttling attributes.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: HopIDs start at 8; -1 requests automatic allocation; 0 deallocates while the stream is idle; unavailable explicit IDs return -EBUSY.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: The ring-size range is 32..4096 with default 256; throttling defaults to 8192 ns and accepts 0..16776960 ns.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: USB4STREAM creates TX and RX rings together, enables both tunnel directions, and mandates end-to-end flow control.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: USB4STREAM uses tunneled START PDF 1, DATA PDF 2 and CLOSE PDF 3; DATA is at most 4096 bytes and CLOSE allocates 256 bytes.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: The driver allocates one kernel page per ring slot, DMA-maps it, and copies to/from userspace with iov_iter page-copy helpers.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: Blocking open waits for a matching stream service; O_NONBLOCK open without one returns -ENXIO; invalid HopIDs return -EINVAL.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: Multiple opens share one stream and one pair of rings; readers compete for bytes and writers serialize under the same device lock.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: read_iter blocks for data, returns -EAGAIN in nonblocking mode, permits partial-frame reads and coalescing, and returns EOF after CLOSE or removal is observed.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: write_iter blocks for TX availability, returns -EAGAIN in nonblocking mode, chunks at 4096 bytes, and may return a positive short write when ring space is exhausted.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: poll reports readable/writable ring availability and reports HUP|ERR only when tbstream_dev_valid() fails; it does not directly test closed or removed flags.

label: [EVIDENCE-GAP]
claim: Durable poll/epoll readiness after peer CLOSE or ConfigFS removal requires machine qualification because the wakeup key and returned poll mask are not the same condition.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: RX CRC and buffer-overrun flags are logged; the callback does not expose a userspace status structure or errno and does not wake readers on the errored frame.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: The final close sends one CLOSE request, ignores its return value, flushes TX and RX for up to 500 ms each, disables paths and frees rings.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: Peer detach wakes waiters and preserves ConfigFS objects; a future matching service can attach, while suspend stops open streams and resume attempts to restart them.

label: [EVIDENCE-GAP]
claim: Reconnect continuity, byte loss and ordering across detach/re-attach or suspend/resume are not guaranteed by documentation and were not machine-tested.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: v7.2-rc3 maps each stream buffer with TB_MAX_FRAME_SIZE but unmaps using the current frame payload size.

label: [BACKPORTED]
claim: The accepted fixes-branch patch changes stream DMA unmap size to TB_MAX_FRAME_SIZE.

label: [EVIDENCE-GAP]
claim: The individual fixes-branch commit object ID was not independently recovered; the patch, blob delta, acceptance and fixes-branch head are pinned.

label: [UNSUPPORTED]
claim: USB4STREAM does not implement registered userspace buffers.

label: [UNSUPPORTED]
claim: USB4STREAM does not implement a driver mmap file operation.

label: [UNSUPPORTED]
claim: USB4STREAM does not implement driver splice methods, dma-buf import/export, uring_cmd or a native zero-copy UAPI.

label: [UNSUPPORTED]
claim: USB4STREAM does not implement GPU-direct or peer-to-peer GPU memory registration.

label: [UNSUPPORTED]
claim: USB4STREAM does not expose a directional-stream preference; each opened stream provisions both directions.

label: [EVIDENCE-GAP]
claim: No public evidence was found for USB4STREAM interoperability with a non-Linux implementation.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: USB4STREAM and thunderbolt-net can coexist and use distinct service/ring resources.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: thunderbolt-net exposes an Ethernet netdevice and fragments packets into 4096-byte DMA frames with a 12-byte header and 4084-byte payload.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: thunderbolt-net supports MTU 68..65522 and a 64 KiB protocol-frame ceiling.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: thunderbolt-net uses 256-entry rings, NAPI receive processing, GRO on completed reassembly, and TSO/SG/checksum feature advertisement.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: thunderbolt-net end-to-end flow control is enabled by default but negotiated with the peer, unlike USB4STREAM where E2E is mandatory.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: thunderbolt-net records CRC, overrun, length, missed and aggregate RX/TX errors through netdevice statistics paths.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: thunderbolt-net statistic units are asymmetric: TX packet accounting is skb-oriented while RX packet accounting advances per accepted USB4NET DMA frame.

label: [EVIDENCE-GAP]
claim: The return values of some receive replenish/poll support calls are not surfaced as a dedicated user-visible error channel; operational impact requires fault injection.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: thunderbolt-net login/logout, carrier, queue, workqueue, NAPI and ring teardown are serialized through its connection lifecycle; suspend detaches and tears down a running netdevice.

label: [PROPOSED]
claim: A 2026 mailing-list proposal to enlarge thunderbolt-net rings/NAPI behavior is not part of v7.2-rc3 released behavior.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: Linux MPTCP defaults to enabled=1, path_manager=kernel and scheduler=default.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: MPTCP close_timeout defaults to 60 seconds and bounds the MPTCP-level make-after-break interval after the last subflow disappears.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: MPTCP stale_loss_cnt defaults to 4; because the implementation tests stale_count > limit, stale transition can occur on the fifth counted no-progress retransmission interval when another active subflow is healthier.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: stale_loss_cnt=0 disables the stale-subflow transition.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: syn_retrans_before_tcp_fallback defaults to 2; the initial MP_CAPABLE SYN and two retransmissions retain MPTCP before a subsequent plain-TCP attempt is allowed.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: An MPTCP listener can accept a peer that does not negotiate MP_CAPABLE as ordinary TCP.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: Failure of an additional subflow is a path-level failure and does not itself convert an established MPTCP connection to ordinary TCP.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: Established fallback or reset depends on specific MP_CAPABLE, DSS/mapping and protocol-error conditions.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: The default scheduler prefers eligible active subflows over backup subflows and considers queued data, pacing, window, memory and burst constraints.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: The fallback scheduler uses the first subflow.

label: [RELEASED]
claim: The kernel path manager and userspace path manager are distinct modes exposed through MPTCP controls and the mptcp_pm generic-netlink family.

label: [NORMATIVE]
claim: RFC 8684 is the standards-track MPTCP baseline and obsoletes RFC 6824.

label: [NORMATIVE]
claim: RFC 8684 verified erratum 6609 is part of the normative evidence set.

label: [NORMATIVE]
claim: USB4 v2.0 November 2025 is the selected public USB4 specification package metadata baseline.

label: [EVIDENCE-GAP]

label: [NORMATIVE]
claim: USB Type-C Release 2.5 is the selected cable/connector baseline metadata.

label: [EVIDENCE-GAP]
claim: PCIe Base Specification 7.0 normative text is member/license controlled; only public overview and errata/ECN metadata were accessible.
